verdict.rationale_short: Iran fired ballistic missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain overnight, severely damaged Kuwait airport, and struck an oil tanker near Kuwait port; Brent climbs toward the $97 mandatory XLE-stub cover trigger. Dow futures are -180 points on the Iran bid. Note: the June 2 night brief misstated the close — the S&P 500 actually closed at a record 7,609.78 (+0.13%), driven by Marvell +25%, NVDA +5.7%, and HPE +25%. The 30Y sits at 4.965% — technical Day-1 of the sub-5.0% sequence, the first constructive rate signal in five sessions — but an Iran-driven oil spike could reverse it before Day-2 confirmation. STEP ASIDE maintained: hold NVDA (stop $215), cover the XLE stub on any Brent close above $97, and watch ADP (8:15 AM ET) and ISM Services PMI (10:00 AM ET) for the labor-market signal.

bear_case: Iran's escalation has moved from a negotiating standoff to kinetic cross-border strikes: ballistic missiles targeted Kuwait and Bahrain, a sea drone struck an oil tanker 800 km from the Strait, and US forces retaliated on Qeshm Island. The Hormuz strait has been closed since March 4; Iran is now expanding the conflict horizontally into Gulf states that were previously outside the blast radius. Brent at the $97 trigger means oil is re-embedding inflation at exactly the moment the 30Y needs a Day-2 sub-5.0% print to support any upgrade thesis — those two dynamics are directly in conflict. The S&P 500 sits at a record 7,609.78 with a forward PE of 22.66x (83rd percentile of the 10-year range), carried by a shrinking set of AI leaders while crypto sends a divergent risk-off signal at $67K. A Brent close above $97 combined with a reversal in the 30Y back above 5.05% converts STEP ASIDE to BEARISH — exit all longs. Invalidation of the bear-upgrade trigger: if Brent retreats to $92 AND the 30Y confirms Day-2 below 5.0%, the framework upgrades to HOLD.
